name: Latvia
summary_text: Latvia is broadly workable with no legal framework for gender recognition — trans people cannot legally change their gender marker, leaving those who've transitioned in a legal limbo. The most documented institutional failure is the European Court of Human Rights ruling Hanovs v. Latvia (2024), which found Latvia failed to prosecute a homophobic hate crime (the 2021 attack on lecturer Deniss Hanovs), violating the prohibition of inhuman treatment and the right to private life. There is no criminalisation, and bathrooms are unrestricted. On the positive side, an administrative court overturned the denial of asylum to a Ghanaian LGBTI asylum-seeker in 2025, showing some institutional capacity for protection. The documented hostility is less extreme than in Lithuania (no "degenerate"-rhetoric MP, no propaganda-style minors law, no systemic-trans-workplace-harassment study surfaced), which places Latvia marginally above its southern neighbour.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying LSM article (June 2025) covers transgender and non-binary Latvians facing a struggle for recognition.

ECtHR press release, Hanovs v. Latvia (18 July 2024): the Court unanimously found violations of Articles 3, 8 and 14 after a 2020 homophobic attack - no criminal charges were brought despite the aggressor admitting anti-gay slurs; the case was downgraded to a minor public-order matter with a lenient fine, fostering impunity for hate-motivated offences.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on Latvia: an administrative court overturned denial of asylum to a Ghanaian LGBTI seeker; the Prosecutor General reopened criminal proceedings in the Khanov hate-crime case after the ECtHR ruling; two people attacked in Daugavpils, with the Prosecutor General ordering the investigation reopened after police closed it; former MEP Mamikins' homophobic posts investigated (he fled to Russia).

sources.title: Hanovs v. Latvia: Further clarification of the positive obligations of States in cases involving homophobic attacks - Strasbourg Observers
sources.claim_summary: Strasbourg Observers analysis (Nov 2024) of Hanovs v. Latvia: further clarification of states' positive obligations in homophobic-attack cases - states must thoroughly investigate and punish hate crimes, sending a message of zero tolerance; notes the troubling pattern of Eastern European states failing to protect LGBTI+ persons and to investigate effectively.

sources.title: European court finds Latvia failed to protect victim of homophobic attack court finds
sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Latvia page: includes the July 2024 ECtHR judgment in Hanovs v. Latvia - the Court found violations of Articles 3, 8 and 14 after Latvian authorities declined to prosecute a homophobic assault on a gay couple in Riga as a hate-motivated offence.

sources.title: Cardinal: homosexuality a form of prostitution | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (May 2007): Archbishop of Riga Cardinal Janis Pujats called homosexuality 'total corruption in the sexual arena' and 'an unnatural form of prostitution', demanded a referendum on same-sex marriage and crowds of 40,000-50,000 to counter Pride, calling Pride a 'foreign-inspired action'.
Xinhua (June 2018): around 8,000 people marched in Baltic Pride 2018 in Riga - the annual event rotated among Baltic capitals; organised by Mozaika under the motto 'See Diversity! See Freedom!'.
